featured_reviews.name: Bangkokian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a great dining experience at Ferry Wharf Seafood Restaurant – Bandra Reclamation (West) and really enjoyed every dish. 🦀🦞

The seafood was very fresh, and it was nice to see the selection before cooking. We tried several dishes, and everything was delicious, well cooked, and full of flavor. The crab, prawns, and fish were especially good fresh, tender, and perfectly seasoned.

The staff were friendly and helpful, and the overall atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable. You can really tell that this restaurant focuses on quality seafood and good taste.

If you love seafood and are looking for a reliable place in Bandra, I highly recommend Ferry Wharf. I would definitely come back again.

featured_reviews.name: Taara Todkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great experience at this restaurant today with Kielash. We ordered an array of seafood and other foods - sukkah crab, tandoori chicken, bombil, bangda fry (mackerel) and seafood biryani.

The crab and bombil were amazing both flavourful and rich - would highly recommend! The seafood biryani was good and the tandoori chicken was moist and delicious. Our only issue with the food today was the mackerel as although the masala was nice the fish itself did not taste as fresh.

Service was amazing as the employees were very helpful.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. CHAITANYA JASTI
featured_reviews.review_text: As the street amazes you with some great eateries, Ferry Wharf satisfies you with some good dishes to offer. Seafood here is specail and the coconur base Prawn gravy is a must try with appam (Tiffin Box).  The bamboo biriyani seems to be popular here, but for someone who is well versed with the authentic bamboo biriyani from eastern ghats, doesn't find this satisfying, though a decent attempt.

I visited Ferry Wharf few days ago on a weekday. I found it not too busy, very comfortable and aesthetics are great as well of the restaurant.

Being a vegetarian, I ordered Cream Brocolli, Cheese Stuffed Potatoes as starters and dal and rice for mains. I would like to recommend the Brocolli starter and the cheese naan is to die for!

My non-vegetarian company tried prawns fish thali, rava fish fry and chicken kebabs along with some other dishes. But everything in non-veg section was amazing. The staff also let us pick up a crab for pictures.

The staff paid attention to our needs and were very good hosts! Loved my experience. Won't mind visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: Merlyn
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had originally checked with Soul Fry for their karaoke nights, but the owner mentioned that reservations usually need to be made around 10 days to 2 weeks in advance. Later, we ended up going there for lunch on one of the days. I had even called beforehand to ask if reservations were necessary, and he said yes, definitely. But when we actually reached, the restaurant was pretty empty.

The food was good — nothing extremely standout, but overall decent. One thing we did feel though was that everything was slightly on the pricier side for what was offered. That being said, the interiors really give you that old-school Goan tavern vibe, which added a nice charm to the experience.

featured_reviews.name: george joseph
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find. A cute little restaurant with goan vibes right in bandra. You would need to plan to be there around opening time if you want to get a seat in their cozy indoor area. They close for the evening making it a little exclusive with the time restriction. The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Ashwinth Naveen
featured_reviews.review_text: My first time in Mumbai, and I have absolutely no regrets choosing Soul Fry as my go-to spot! The karaoke night was an absolute blast and made the whole experience even more memorable. The vibe, music, and overall atmosphere were amazing, and I genuinely had such a great time. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip — would love to visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.name: Nataleigh Lasrado
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Fresh Catch on 4 June 2026 and it was excellent!  I asked the bartender to create me a great custom drink and he exceeded my expectations with refreshing and unique creations. My waiter, Lawrence, was extremely helpful in bombil suggestions as well as sourcing from off menu fish. Try Fresh Catch you won’t be disappointed with the drinks, food or service. Ask for Lawrence!

featured_reviews.name: Avinash D'Souza
featured_reviews.review_text: Fresh Catch by Francis is located on the 2nd Floor. Lift available. Had the Prawn pulao and Surmai Rossa Curry with Bombil rava fry. Delicious food and good quality for 2 people

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Bose
featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

featured_reviews.name: Sushant Khadpe
featured_reviews.review_text: 14 Sept Sunday - note - most of positive reviews are fake be aware - This so-called restaurant is nothing but a disgraceful dump masquerading as a place to eat , we entered at 2:30 pm in the AC section and left at 4:45 pm, not because we were gossiping but because these jokers took 25 minutes to serve each dish even after repeatedly calling them while restaurant is not in rush hour 20% capacity guest was there , stretching the ordeal into hours of torture. First insult came when I asked for a non-veg thali at 3:15 pm, only to be casually told it was “finished,” but twenty minutes later my friend caught them serving that same thali to another family; embarrassed, they suddenly claimed the thali “started again,” so we reordered, and guess what—they had the audacity to dump a prawns thali on our table without even the curry. Drinks were thrown on our table with the elegance of a desi daru theka, no service, no manners, no sense of hospitality. The food that finally limped its way to our table was tasteless garbage not worth a single rupee, basic spoons and tissues were missing, and I had to snatch them off a nearby table like a beggar. Shame turned into rage when we saw an elderly couple waiting endlessly, only to leave without food, ignored by the careless staff walking around like clueless zombies under the command of an equally worthless owner. After paying ₹3400 for 3 person - for this circus of clowns, what we got was hell’s own dining corner, a rotten scam of mismanagement, cruelty, and disgust that should be shut down immediately, because stepping into this filthy disaster is an insult to anyone’s self-respect.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Undoubtedly one of the finest seafood experiences we had in Mumbai. Tucked away on Hill Road, the restaurant is conveniently located and easy to reach. While the space itself is compact, the team handles the steady crowd with remarkable efficiency.
We opted for the Surumai (Kingfish) thali, beautifully paired with soft neer dosa, steamed rice, and a deeply flavorful fish gassi, and complemented it with the indulgent prawns ghee roast. Every dish stood out for its freshness, balance of spices, and impeccable execution. The service was attentive and warm, further elevating the overall experience.
What truly impresses is the value — exceptionally affordable for the quality offered, especially by Mumbai standards. A must-visit for seafood connoisseurs.

description: Malvani Kkalwan is an authentic Malvani restaurant and seafood specialist in Aram Nagar, Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai. Known across the city for our signature sol kadi and Konkani seafood, this is genuine Malvani food the way Kokan Katta intended, with dishes like fish curry, surmai, bombil fry, kombdi vade, and prawns, mutton, and surmai thalis served with bhakri, chapati, and amboli on the side. A true Konkani restaurant for Mumbai seafood lovers, we bring coastal Malvani flavours straight to your table, the same way it has been made for generations along the Konkan coast. Easy to find on JP Road, near Seven Bungalows Garden, and close to Versova, Lokhandwala, and Yari Road. Come taste authentic Malvani food, the real Konkani way, today.

owner_posts.post_text:
The Surmai Fish Thali at Malwani Kkalwan is the meal that makes the case for authentic Malvani food Mumbai before the first bite even reaches the table — surmai fried to a proper crisp, a sharp Malvani fish curry built on coconut and kokum, served alongside bhakri, chapati, amboli, and steamed rice in the kind of full spread that a one-dish order simply cannot replicate on its own no matter how good that single dish happens to be on its own merit alone. This is Konkani coastal cooking the way it has been made for generations along the Konkan coast, not a shortened version built for speed and convenience at the cost of flavour.

It sits at the centre of why Malwani Kkalwan continues to hold a genuinely strong position for authentic Malvani food Mumbai — a thali built around surmai rather than assembled from whatever happened to be available that particular day, served at an address in Aram Nagar that has become the destination for seafood lovers across Versova, Lokhandwala, Yari Road, and Andheri West. Sol Kadi on the side rounds out the meal exactly the way it should, cooling the palate between every bite of fish curry along the way through the entire meal served.

For anyone searching for authentic Malvani food Mumbai or an authentic Konkani restaurant Mumbai with a proper fish thali worth the trip across the city — Malwani Kkalwan on JP Road, near Seven Bungalows Garden, is that address.

The thali will have a fried Surmai, a Surmai curry with surmai fish in that too, sole curry, nice daal, papad, a yummy "brinjal jevala" and rice hand breads and steamed rice.

Our tummies were full, but our hearts weren't.
so we ordered for the dessert ... a sweet caramel custard.

It made our hearts melt with joy !!!

Finally our meal here was over, but made us want to come back again for more !!!

The second time we ate Bangda and Rawas thalis. Both were amazing. The bangda fish was so good we ended up ordering a second order of 2 bangda frys. Another 10/10.

Had modak as dessert which was also soft, juicy and just lovely. The kokam soda is also the best way to cleanse your palate.

In closing I would like to say, if you have any desire to eat seafood, this place is a blind go. You cannot go wrong with anything you order. 100/10.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has such an amazing tropical ambience. You are welcomed by soulful Goan music, and the vibe is relaxed and unhurried. The servers don’t rush you, making it a perfect spot to truly enjoy your meal.

Mr. Merwin, the manager, took great care of us, and our servers Sonia and Edwin were humble, polite, and very prompt, obliging us with every request.

The food is unlike anything you’ve tasted.. authentic Goan cuisine rooted deeply in the culture and spices of Goa. Every dish is beautifully presented, with thoughtful plating that elevates the experience without being overdone. The cutlery, plates, and glassware are aesthetically pleasing and enhance the dining experience, without robbing you of quantity. Portions are generous and satisfying.

From the big plates, we had the Traditional Pork Sorpatel with rice, Goan-style chilli chicken, and Surmai fish curry rice. The sorpatel was so authentic it made my mum emotional...it brought back memories of old friends who had cooked traditional pork dishes in her younger days. The Goan-style chilli chicken was the standout dish of the afternoon...smooth, succulent, and packed with a powerful flavour punch. The surmai fish curry rice felt like something an old granny had made, warm, comforting, and soulful.

From the small plates, we tried the Goan fried chicken with spicy mayo...six generous boneless strips, made to order, pairing perfectly with lime and the spicy mayo. The grilled squid stuffed with crab was outstanding, with the masala truly stealing the show. The prawn balchao masala stuffed forminhas crispy tarts were tangy and well-made; while not my personal favourite, they were only overshadowed by stronger dishes. The tender coconut and raw mango salad was light, tropical, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.

For drinks, we had the Coconut Boy Refresher, Kokum Spritz, and Tamarind Trails. These are not your usual cocktails... Goan spices and flavours take centre stage, and an open mind is needed to fully enjoy them.

Coconut Boy truly lives up to its promise of 'fresh' and delivers an experience that transports you straight to Goa. Highly recommended even if you’re simply looking for some relaxed downtime with exceptional food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Everything On A Plate EOAP
featured_reviews.review_text:
AMBIENCE:

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm. The cost is a bit on the higher end but the quality and flavors are worth every penny.

featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Subodh, 
Experiencing the flavors of the Konkan coast is truly what dining is all about, and it’s wonderful to hear that our seafood dishes resonated with you. The Bombil Fry and Butter Garlic Pepper Crab are favorites for a reason, and it’s delightful to know they stood out during your visit. Your pro tip about the "Catch of the Day" is sure to help other guests maximize their experience!
Regards, 
Mahesh Lunch Home

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found this hidden gem in Marol and what an experience! Nav Gomantak brings the true coastal flavors right to Mumbai.

What I tried:
Bharlela Bombil (Chutney) - Absolutely stellar! The stuffed bombil was perfectly spiced and the chutney complemented it beautifully. A must-try!

Prawns Koliwada - Crispy, flavorful, and addictive. The coating was perfect and the prawns were fresh and juicy.

Kairiche Panha - Refreshing and authentic raw mango drink. Perfect to balance the spicy food!

Kokum Sarbat - Cool and tangy, exactly what you need with coastal food.

Pomfret Thali - Fresh fish, perfectly cooked with authentic Konkan-style preparation. The thali was wholesome and satisfying.

Chulivarcha Chicken - Traditional chulha-style preparation that brings out the smoky flavors. Outstanding!

Tandalachi Bhakri & Solkadhi - The perfect accompaniment to complete the coastal experience.

The food quality is top-notch, portions are generous, and the authenticity is unmatched. Service was prompt and courteous. If you're craving genuine Konkan cuisine without traveling to the coast, this is THE place!

Highly recommended for seafood lovers!!

Location: Easy to find in Marol, opposite CISL Police Camp
Value for money: Excellent!

Will definitely be coming back for more!!

featured_reviews.name: Adrian Rodrigues
featured_reviews.review_text:
Amazing place if you love to Sea Food. They have an ala carte menu but are best know for their Thali service. If you are not a big water their single dishes are also very tasty. Their sea food is fresh and well prepared. They have a good choice of starters and mains.Everything we ordered was enjoyable.
Their Bombil Fry is a must have.
Captain Lalit was very helpful and professional with his service and even offered us some complimentary Paan Shots.
The seating and ambience is really nice and comfortable.

There is no valet parking but you can find parking on the street opposite the restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Charvi Korgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Nav Gomantak is my go-to hogging place! They serve amazing fish thalis, even the veg food was good and the service is always excellent—special thanks to Vikas and Santosh for being so warm and attentive.

featured_reviews.name: Shane Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: William Gonsalves
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sharing my honest and no filter review. Visited this place with my friend on Tuesday, 9th June after filtering Sai Palace out.
We went on a weekday and unfortunately the tandoor wasn't available from Monday to Friday. It was disheartening to hear tha bcz we wanted to order prawns tandoori. Now that we had already sat on the table we tried to run through the Food Menu. I asked the server, for possible options in non veg starters since tandoor wasn't available and I was surprised to hear that Ghee roast is a starter item and not a main course. On asking the reason the server responded that at Nav Gomantak they treat it as starters. None the less we ordered Prawns Ghee Roast and Bombil Fry. Prawns were 80% cooked and bombil fry had no salt and taste. One word "pathetic". For main course we ordered Chulvarcha mutton and Jeera rice and i was surprised to hear Chulvarcha Mutton (mutton prepared on coal/wood fire) is prepared on gas they has just named it Chulvarcha. Again below average taste mostly over Burnt. Could taste the burnt masala rather than fried. We couldn't finish the mutton and hers rice and packed it and took it with us.
Next day my mother ate the mutton dish and she too said the same thing.
So the restaurant is over hyped. The food is no influence of malvani cuisine let alone Goan cuisine. Spent 2000 for the food, experience 3/10.
Fancy seats, bright lightings or good looking cutlery doesn't guarantee you good and VFM food is what Nav Gomantak taught us. Skipping this restaurant forever. Hope the owners read my comment and improve the food quality.
The 4.3 rating is just a scam

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!

featured_reviews.name: saumya poddar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goh jia Ting - restaurant in bandra, had been on our list for a while, so after a show, we decided to finally give it a try. To be honest, walking into an almost empty restaurant was a little concerning. We were only the second occupied table, and the place remained virtually vacant throughout our visit. Still, we were extremely hungry and the overwhelmingly positive reviews online convinced us to stay and order.

Unfortunately, things went downhill from there.

One of the strangest parts of the evening was the service. At one point, a staff member stood directly in front of our table, watching us eat for an uncomfortably long time. It wasn’t attentive service—it felt intrusive and awkward. She only moved after we specifically requested her to. It genuinely made us uncomfortable, as though we were being monitored rather than hosted.

When I requested disposable chopsticks, the staff said they had them but then handed me what looked like a stranded stirrers and then later confessed that they don’t have disposable chopstick, then why say yes at the first place. Super careless and unprofessional.

The food was even worse. The prawn tempura roll tasted like it had been fried in old, stale oil. Instead of gyoza, we were served something that resembled chicken momos. The lobster roll was completely inedible and was left untouched after a few bites.

The cocktail we ordered, made with star fruit, was equally disappointing. It was so bad that we replaced it with a simple whisky just to avoid any more unpleasant surprises.

After struggling through the starters, we decided not to risk ordering anything else and left for another restaurant to have dinner. The entire experience felt like a complete waste of money.

What started as a restaurant we were genuinely excited to try ended up being one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in Bandra. Between the awkward service, poor food quality, disappointing drinks, and overall lacklustre experience, we left wondering how the glowing reviews online could possibly reflect what we experienced.

There are far too many great dining options in Bandra to spend your time and money here.

featured_reviews.review_text:
PLEASE DO NOT VISIT, would not recommend at all.

We had a 10:00 PM reservation and were only seated at 11:00 PM after standing inside the restaurant for an hour in complete chaos. What’s the point of making a booking? There was absolutely no system to manage reservations or waiting guests — no clarity on who came first, no communication, just a crowded, irritated room full of people arguing. For a place that markets itself as “fancy,” the management was shockingly poor.

Once seated, it didn’t get better. No water or napkins were served until halfway through our meal. We had to ask multiple times for something as basic as a spoon — which still never came. Service felt careless and disorganized throughout.

We ordered black bean veggies but were served some butter garlic gravy that tasted purely of cornstarch — no salt, no flavor, completely inedible. By 11:30 PM we were so hungry and frustrated that we didn’t even bother asking for it to be changed, but it was honestly one of the worst dishes we’ve had.

To top it off, we had to ask for the bill three times, and even then it took 20 minutes. Zero regard for guests’ time.

Completely ruined our evening. When you’re paying premium prices at a so-called upscale restaurant, basic service, organization, and edible food should not be too much to expect. Would not recommend.

To make matters worse, we ordered an LIT (Long Island Iced Tea) cocktail and found a cockroach in it. This is completely unacceptable and raises serious concerns about hygiene standards.
Overall:

Service: Very poor
Staff knowledge: Poor
Hygiene: Unacceptable
Portion size: Small

Good food alone cannot compensate for poor service, lack of transparency, and serious hygiene issues. Finding a cockroach in a cocktail completely ruined the experience.
Would not recommend until major improvements are made in service, staff training, and cleanliness.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Last weekend, I had the pleasure of dining at a delightful local restaurant that truly exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm smiles and genuine hospitality. The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive without being overbearing, which immediately set a welcoming tone for the evening.

The restaurant itself was neat, well-organized, and spotless—a rare and refreshing sight these days. Tables were clean, the atmosphere was cozy, and even the washrooms were well-maintained.

I ordered the mutton biryani and a lime soda, and both were absolutely spot-on. The biryani was aromatic and flavorful, with tender chunks of mutton that fell apart effortlessly. The spices were perfectly balanced—not too overpowering, but enough to leave a lasting impression. The lime soda was refreshing, tangy, and the perfect companion to the rich biryani.

What really stood out, aside from the great food, was how reasonably priced everything was. It's hard to find such quality and cleanliness at such affordable rates these days. Overall, this place is a gem for anyone looking for tasty food, a clean setting, and top-notch service without breaking the bank. I’ll definitely be coming back—and bringing friends along next time.
